[EFFECT]
Temperature has a strong, non-monotonic (inverted-U) effect on hourly bike demand. Starting from very cold temperatures (around 1°C), the contribution is sharply negative — meaning demand is well below the model's baseline — and it rises steadily as temperatures warm up, crossing into positive territory at roughly 18°C. The contribution peaks at around 31°C (normalised value ≈ 0.76), where it adds the most to predicted demand. Beyond that point the effect weakens and turns negative again above approximately 38°C, suggesting that extreme heat also discourages rentals.

[IMPORTANCE]
Temperature is the **second most important** feature in the model out of nine, with an importance score of 0.25. Only the hour of the day outranks it, making temperature a dominant driver of demand.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Plan for the highest bike availability and staffing around mild-to-warm days (roughly 18–31°C); on unusually cold days or during heatwaves, expect noticeably lower ridership and scale resources accordingly.
